text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The European Parliament votes to freeze funds to Turkey.

- Centre-right Diko and right-wing Disy will decide next week on possibility of cooperation in municipal elections, while differences remain between communist Akel and socialist Edek on their own pact.
- President Glafcos Clerides sends his reply to Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash on the Turkish side's rejection of demilitarisation.
- Amnesty proposed as a solution to the problem of illegal labour is given the cold shoulder in parliament.
- Parliament moots the possibility of creating a blacklist for bouncing cheques.
- The government laughs off a smear campaign against President Clerides by Turkish Cypriots in the UK.
- Parliament blasts attempts by a media organisation to undermine work of the House by drawing paralells between the number of police guarding MPs and criminals.
- Freak storms in Limassol, Paphos and Larnaca cause around nine million pounds in damage.
- "I would be a hypocrite if I adressed you as 'Dear Rauf'," Clerides says, using unusually harsh language in his reply to Denktash.
- The government continues its contacts with employers and trade unions over the incorporation of the cost of living allowance into salaries, but a resolution does not appear to be in sight.
- Parliamentarians lash out at media disclosures on the number of bodyguards they have.
- Clerides blames Denktash for the murders of Greek Cypriots earlier this year.
